props.raw: Advanced Programming

A second programming course that moves students from writing small single-file programs to building larger applications made of several components with clear interfaces. Students learn object-oriented design, how to write code that others can reuse and test, how to structure programs around established design patterns, and how to handle errors, input/output and concurrency. By the end, students working in pairs can take a reasonably well-specified application design and deliver a working, tested, multi-component program. Java is the vehicle, but the course is about program design, not the Java language.

props.summary: CS 108 introduces software design and construction using large object‑oriented Java libraries. The course covers OOP design principles, design patterns, testing, GUI libraries, and software‑engineering strategies for team programming.

The course equips students with systematic and rigorous software development skills, covering requirements, design, implementation, quality assurance and project management within an object‑oriented paradigm. It emphasizes hands‑on experience with industry‑standard tools such as test automation, build automation and code revisioning. The workload combines lectures, tutorials and substantial project work.

The course introduces the concept of abstraction and its application in programming, emphasizing data abstraction, modularity, and object‑oriented design. It covers fundamental data structures, recursion, and basic algorithmic analysis using the C++ language.

props.summary: This accelerated Stanford course introduces engineering of computer applications using modern software engineering principles such as object‑oriented design, decomposition, encapsulation, abstraction and testing. It is aimed at students with prior programming experience, allowing deeper coverage of the material.

The course introduces software design principles focusing on decomposing large systems into maintainable classes. It covers causes of complexity, modular design, deep‑class techniques, exception handling, documentation and naming, and is delivered in a studio format with iterative implementation, reviews and code reviews.
topics: studio format with in‑class discussions and code reviews

props.summary: The course involves a team‑based software development project where students design, specify, implement and test a substantial application under faculty supervision. Deliverables include a project rationale, design documentation, weekly progress logs, and a software architecture diagram, culminating in a public demonstration at the quarter’s end.
